name: Semillon
old_value: A white grape that once covered most of the Cape's vineyards. It gives fuller bodied wines, and in South Africa it is closely tied to Franschhoek.
new_value: A white grape that gives fuller bodied wines with a waxy texture and lemon notes, often blended with Sauvignon Blanc. It is the main grape of sweet Sauternes, and in the Hunter Valley it makes light, dry wines that age for decades.
note: Removed (South Africa specific, move to the Franschhoek region note): "A white grape that once covered most of the Cape's vineyards." and "in South Africa it is closely tied to Franschhoek." Neither was verified in this pass (Wine Folly alone says it was once the most planted grape there; nothing found for Franschhoek), so verify with WOSA before the region note uses them. "Low acidity" deliberately left out: sources disagree.

new_value: An aromatic Muscat grape, called Moscatel in Portugal and Spain, with floral and orange notes. It is used mostly for sweet and fortified wines such as Moscatel de Setúbal, and is also made into dry, aromatic whites.

name: Pinot Blanc
old_value: A white grape called Weissburgunder in Austria. It gives dry wines with citrus and stone fruit notes and a mineral edge, usually made to drink young.
new_value: A white grape called Weissburgunder in Germany and Austria and Pinot Bianco in Italy. It gives light, fresh dry wines with gentle pear, peach and lemon notes, and is also used for sparkling wine such as Crémant d'Alsace.
note: Removed (Austria specific framing): "A white grape called Weissburgunder in Austria." kept as part of a general naming clause, so nothing needs to move.
